Dew rested on the grass like tiny cold silver beads

A newspaper fluttered down from a high and open window

Shoes clicked on the stone with steady quick bright rhythm
A bell rang once and then it rang twice again
The city remembered that quiet morning and held it close

Rain had washed the leaves until they shone like glass
Branches bowed gently toward the street with very soft weight
A dog shook water from its fur in a spray
Its owner called a name that carried far down street
Pigeons gathered on the ledge to share a bread crumb
A musician played violin near the fountain in the square
Notes drifted upward, then gently settled on the wet stone
A woman stopped, closed her eyes, and listened very hard
Children pointed at the clouds, which looked like strange animals

The fountain sparkled under light with a bright silver ring

A bench held two strangers, both watching the same scene

A letter sat folded on an empty bus seat, waiting

Words on the page might change a very quiet day
The train came in with a low and steady hum
Passengers stepped forward toward the bright and wide open doors
One man carried a violin case like his own child

A woman asked softly if he would play for them
He smiled and said yes with a very slow nod
The case opened, and the strings appeared in the light
First note sounded small, then slowly grew into a memory
The room grew still as the melody began to move
A small child tapped her foot to the music rhythm
An old man closed his eyes and remembered his home
A young couple held hands beneath a window of rain
The violin softly spoke of places no map could find

Maybe a field, maybe a shore, maybe an open door
The train waited, then started, then disappeared behind the hill
The station kept its echo for a quiet little while
A clock ticked near the wall with very patient patience
People checked their phones, then quietly put them away again
A woman sold bright oranges from a big wooden crate
Their color glowed like small suns in the dim light
A boy bought one and held it in his palm
The juice ran down his wrist, sweet and very bright
He laughed and ran toward the fountain with the sun

The fountain caught his shadow and gently gave it back
A bird landed on the rim and tilted its head
It pecked at the water with a sharp bright beak
A man took a photo, then soon forgot about it
The screen glowed in his hand for a few seconds
Then he looked up at the sky and breathed again
A cloud moved across the moon like a slow ship
The square was full of small and very simple sounds
A laugh, a bell, a dog, a bus brake hum
The night arrived softly, wearing a bright coat of stars

Street lamps lit one by one along the long avenue
People walked home with coats pulled tight against the chill
A cafe opened its doors and spilled bright warm light
Cups clinked inside, and stories began to warm the room
A waiter wiped a table with a very patient hand
A child drew a horse with a long thin neck
She used a crayon red as the bright setting sun
Her mother watched quietly from a chair by the window
Outside, the rain had returned, but only for a while
It tapped the glass like fingers asking to be in

The city dreamed beneath its lights with a slow heartbeat
Every window held a face, a hope, or a book
One man read a long novel about a lost island
His chair creaked, but he did not look up yet
A page turned in the wind at the shop window
The letter from the bus had vanished completely by now
Maybe it had been read, maybe it had been kept
Time quietly did not care which ending it had chosen
The violin case closed, but the music stayed there behind
A woman hummed the tune while walking to the gate

The gate opened onto a road lined with old trees
Leaves whispered softly as she passed beneath their silver branches
She carried a cup of tea, still warm in hand
The steam rose like a question into the dark air
A star appeared above the roof, then another, then more
The city kept its secrets in the space between lights
It kept its songs in the pause between two notes
It kept its rain in the memory of green leaves
And in the morning, the quiet streets would begin again
The rain stopped slowly under a grey and quiet sky
